criterion_name: Implantable Cardioverter Defibrillators (ICDs) — medical necessity / coverage criteria
text: Covers ICD implantation for (1) secondary prevention - patients with a personal history of sustained ventricular tachyarrhythmia (VT) or cardiac arrest due to ventricular fibrillation (VF); and (2) primary prevention - patients with prior MI and measured LVEF <=0.30-0.35, or non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy (NIDCM) >3 months with NYHA Class II/III heart failure and LVEF <=35% after >=3 months of optimal medical therapy. Patients must be clinically stable and not have NYHA Class IV heart failure (except for CRT indications), a disease with <1 year expected survival, or a recent CABG/PCI or MI within specified waiting periods (with limited exceptions). Shared decision-making is required before implant for primary-prevention patients.
revision_date: Not fixed — CMS revises NCDs on an as-needed basis (last change reflected in version 5)

criterion_name: Implantable Cardioverter Defibrillators (ICDs) — key clinical thresholds
text: LVEF thresholds: <=0.30 (post-MI) / <=35% (NIDCM+NYHA II-III); LVEF measured by echo, nuclear imaging, cardiac MRI, or angiography; 3-month OMT requirement for NIDCM; NYHA Class IV generally excludes coverage (except CRT).
revision_date: Not fixed — CMS revises NCDs on an as-needed basis (last change reflected in version 5)

criterion_name: Mammograms — medical necessity / coverage criteria
text: Screening mammography: covered annually for women age 40+, one baseline exam for ages 35-39, not covered under age 35; each screening exam requires >=11 months since the prior one. Diagnostic mammography: covered when ordered by a physician for a patient with signs/symptoms of breast disease, a personal history of breast cancer, or biopsy-proven benign breast disease.

criterion_name: Colorectal Cancer Screening Tests — medical necessity / coverage criteria
text: Covers several screening modalities for asymptomatic, average-risk beneficiaries: guaiac/immunoassay fecal occult blood test (FOBT) annually (age 45+); multi-target stool DNA test (e.g., Cologuard) once every 3 years (age 45-85, following a 2023 policy update lowering the minimum age); blood-based biomarker test once every 3 years (age 45+, since 01/19/2021). 'Average risk' excludes patients with personal history of adenomatous polyps, colorectal cancer, or inflammatory bowel disease, or family history of colorectal cancer/polyposis syndromes.
exclusions: personal history of adenomatous polyps, colorectal cancer, or inflammatory bowel disease, or family history of colorectal cancer/polyposis syndromes

policy_title: Positron Emission Tomography (FDG) for Oncologic Conditions
criterion_name: Positron Emission Tomography (FDG) for Oncologic Conditions — medical necessity / coverage criteria
text: Covers FDG PET for biopsy-proven or strongly-suspected solid tumors/myeloma to guide the initial anti-tumor treatment strategy (staging, determining candidacy for an invasive procedure, or locating the optimal biopsy site) - contractor discretion applies to any scan beyond the first. Also covers up to three FDG PET scans to guide subsequent management after completion of initial anti-cancer therapy for the same diagnosis; additional scans beyond three are left to local MAC discretion. Coverage does not extend to routine cancer screening in asymptomatic patients.

criterion_name: Total Knee Arthroplasty — medical necessity / coverage criteria
text: Medically necessary when the patient has advanced joint disease shown on radiography (or MRI/CT if radiography is inadequate) - e.g., subchondral cysts/sclerosis, periarticular osteophytes, joint-space narrowing, avascular necrosis - combined with pain or functional disability from trauma or arthritis, and, where appropriate, a documented history of unsuccessful conservative (non-surgical) therapy or documented justification for skipping it. Revision/replacement is separately indicated for component loosening, fracture/mechanical failure, infection, periprosthetic fracture, progressive bone loss, symptomatic wear, malalignment, stiffness/arthrofibrosis, or instability. Not medically necessary in the presence of active joint/systemic infection, active urinary/dental/skin infection or open wound at the surgical site, or rapidly progressive neurological disease.
exclusions: active joint/systemic infection, active urinary/dental/skin infection or open wound at the surgical site, or rapidly progressive neurological disease

criterion_name: Total Joint Arthroplasty — medical necessity / coverage criteria
text: Covers total hip and knee replacement (not unicompartmental knee replacement) under medical-necessity criteria closely aligned with other MAC total-joint LCDs: documented advanced joint disease with imaging support, pain/functional impairment, and conservative-therapy history or justification for bypassing it. Not reasonable and necessary where there is active hip/knee joint or systemic infection, active skin infection or open wound at the planned surgical site, or rapidly progressive neurological disease (except with a concomitant displaced femoral neck fracture).
exclusions: active hip/knee joint or systemic infection, active skin infection or open wound at the planned surgical site, or rapidly progressive neurological disease (except with a concomitant displaced femoral neck fracture)

criterion_name: Breast Imaging Mammography/Breast Echography (Sonography)/Breast MRI/Ductography — medical necessity / coverage criteria
text: Screening mammography covered annually for women 40+, plus one baseline exam ages 35-39 (mirrors NCD 220.4). Breast ultrasound/sonography and MRI are covered for specific diagnostic indications such as characterizing a mammographically-detected or palpable mass, assessing implant integrity, or evaluating suspicious calcifications, generally when mammography alone is inconclusive. Diagnostic tests must be ordered by the treating physician managing the specific problem (42 CFR 410.32); orders from a non-treating provider are not reasonable and necessary.

criterion_name: Advanced hip joint disease meeting THA criteria
text: Total hip arthroplasty is medically necessary for adults with pain and ADL-limiting disability from osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, avascular necrosis, or post-traumatic arthritis, plus limited ROM/antalgic gait/pain on exam, plus radiographic avascular necrosis stage II-III OR Tonnis grade 2-3 osteoarthritis/RA, AND a documented trial of conservative therapy (12 weeks, or 24 weeks if BMI>40 or age<50) including anti-inflammatories, flexibility/strengthening exercises, activity modification, and in-person supervised physical therapy -- confirmed by PT notes or claims history.
limitations: ing disability from osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, avascular necrosis, or post-traumatic arthritis, plus limited ROM/antalgic gait/pain on exam, plus radiographic avascular necrosis stage II-III OR Tonnis grade 2-3 osteoarthritis/RA, AND a documented trial of conservative therapy (12 weeks, or 24 weeks if BMI>40 or age<50) including anti-inflammatories, flexibility/strengthening exercises, activity modification, and in-person supervised physical therapy -- confirmed by PT notes or claims history

criterion_name: THA outside defined criteria is experimental
text: THA is considered experimental/investigational for any indication outside the defined medical-necessity criteria. Revision/removal for post-op metallosis alone, with no evidence of loosening or malposition, is separately excluded for insufficient published evidence.

criterion_name: Facility-based NPSG for pediatric OSA diagnosis
text: Facility-based nocturnal polysomnography is medically necessary for children/adolescents under 18 to diagnose OSAS, evaluate hypersomnia, or investigate suspected narcolepsy, parasomnia, restless leg syndrome, periodic limb movement disorder, congenital central alveolar hypoventilation, or hypoventilation from neuromuscular disease/chest wall deformity. A split-night PAP-titration study is allowed if moderate/severe OSA is confirmed and optimal titration achieved within the first 2 hours plus 3+ hours of titration; otherwise a second night is required.

criterion_name: Adenotonsillectomy as first-line; CPAP as fallback
text: Adenoidectomy and/or tonsillectomy is medically necessary first-line treatment for pediatric OSAS with habitual snoring and an apnea index above 1 on NPSG. CPAP is medically necessary when adenotonsillectomy is contraindicated, delayed, or unsuccessful. FDA-approved hypoglossal nerve stimulation is medically necessary only for adolescents 13-18 with Down syndrome who have AHI 10-50, no complete concentric palatal collapse, are not candidates for/failed adenotonsillectomy, and have documented PAP failure or intolerance.

criterion_name: Bariatric surgery BMI + comorbidity + program criteria
text: RYGB, sleeve gastrectomy, LASGB, BPD/DS, SADI-S, and SIPS are medically necessary for adults (18+) with BMI >=40 (>=37.5 for Asian ancestry) OR BMI >=35 (>=32.5 for Asian ancestry) plus a severe comorbidity (clinically significant OSA, documented coronary heart disease, medically refractory hypertension, type 2 diabetes, or MASH), AND for adolescents who have completed bone growth with BMI >40. The member must also have documented prior unsuccessful weight-loss attempts, a completed intensive multicomponent behavioral intervention (12+ sessions within 2 years pre-surgery covering nutrition/activity/behavior), and a pre-surgical behavioral-health assessment for psychosocial functioning, substance use, and eating behaviors.

criterion_name: Bariatric procedures/uses considered experimental
text: Aetna lists over 40 specific procedures/uses as experimental or investigational, including intragastric balloons, mini gastric bypass, endoscopic sleeve gastroplasty (transoral gastroplasty), gastric plication, VBG outside the narrow comorbidity-driven exception, and bariatric surgery used specifically to treat infertility, rheumatoid arthritis, or type 2 diabetes in patients with BMI under 35 who don't otherwise meet the criteria above.

policy_title: MRI and CT of the Spine
criterion_name: Imaging modality scope and precertification note
text: This CPB covers MRI and CT imaging of the spine. Precertification may be required for select procedures depending on the member's plan; the CPT-code search tool should be checked case by case rather than assuming coverage from this bulletin alone.

policy_title: MRI and CT of the Spine
criterion_name: Radiculopathy / conservative-therapy-failure indication
text: MRI/CT of the spine is medically necessary for persistent back or neck pain WITH radiculopathy -- defined as pain plus objective motor or reflex changes in a specific nerve-root distribution -- that has not improved after 6 weeks of conservative therapy (moderate activity, analgesics, NSAIDs, muscle relaxants), and for spondylolisthesis/degenerative spine disease unresponsive to 4 weeks of the same conservative measures. This is one of 18 listed medically-necessary indications; others include suspected cord compression, spinal stenosis, suspected malignancy or infection, and trauma with suspected fracture.

criterion_name: High genetic-risk screening MRI criteria
text: Breast MRI as an adjunct to mammography is medically necessary for high-genetic-risk screening when the member carries (or has a first-degree relative who carries) a pathogenic mutation in TP53, PTEN, PALB2, STK11/LKB1, CDH1, NF1, ATM, CHEK2, NBN, BARD1, RAD51C, RAD51D, BRCA1, or BRCA2, OR has a calculated lifetime breast-cancer risk of 20-25% or greater by a standard model (BRCAPRO, Claus, Gail, or Tyrer-Cuzick). A mammogram within the past year is required except for women under 30.

criterion_name: Diagnostic / staging indications for known or suspected cancer
text: Breast MRI is separately medically necessary (with a recent mammogram/sonogram on file) for 13 diagnostic circumstances, including staging before/after neoadjuvant chemotherapy, detecting implant rupture in symptomatic patients, evaluating dense/scarred breasts where mammography and ultrasound are limited, localizing occult primary tumors presenting as nodal metastasis, mapping multifocal/multicentric disease, and characterizing inconclusive findings left unresolved after complete mammographic and sonographic work-up.
limitations: ed, localizing occult primary tumors presenting as nodal metastasis, mapping multifocal/multicentric disease, and characterizing inconclusive findings left unresolved after complete mammographic and sonographic work-up

criterion_name: Attended NPSG vs. home sleep testing indications
text: Attended facility-based NPSG (Type I) is medically necessary for adults with symptoms suggestive of OSA who have a comorbidity that degrades home-test accuracy (moderate/severe pulmonary disease, neuromuscular disease, stroke with residual effects, epilepsy, CHF NYHA III/IV, pulmonary hypertension, chronic opioid use, or BMI>45), a comorbid sleep disorder, a negative/inadequate home test, low pretest probability, or an inability to safely use home equipment. Otherwise, unattended home testing with a Type II-IV(A) device (or a 3+-channel Watch-PAT-type device) measuring AHI and oxygen saturation is medically necessary.

criterion_name: CPAP/APAP medical necessity thresholds
text: CPAP/APAP (with or without pressure-relief technology) is medically necessary DME for a positive facility or home sleep test showing AHI/RDI >=15/hour (min. 30 events), OR AHI/RDI 5-14.9/hour (min. 10 events) plus at least one of: documented stroke, hypertension, ischemic heart disease, impaired cognition/mood/insomnia symptoms, Epworth >10, or significant oxygen-desaturation episodes. BiPAP without a backup rate is medically necessary only after documented CPAP/APAP intolerance or ineffectiveness at optimal fit and pressure.

policy_title: Quantitative, Functional and Connectomic Analysis of Brain MRI
criterion_name: fMRI pre-surgical eloquent-cortex mapping (narrow indication)
text: fMRI (CPT 70554/70555) is medically necessary strictly to localize the eloquent cortex before surgery in patients with brain tumors (excluding temporal tumors), epilepsy (excluding temporal neocortical epilepsy), or vascular malformations. All other fMRI uses -- including for Alzheimer's, ADHD, autism, bipolar disorder, chronic pain, disorders of consciousness, migraines, MS, Parkinson's, psychosis, PTSD/trauma, or stroke rehabilitation -- are experimental/investigational, as are quantitative brain-MRI analysis and connectomic analysis of multi-modal brain MRI in general.

criterion_name: Advanced knee joint disease meeting TKA criteria
text: Total knee arthroplasty is medically necessary for adults with ADL-limiting pain and disability from osteoarthritis, RA, avascular necrosis, or post-traumatic arthritis, plus limited ROM/crepitus/effusion on exam, plus radiographic Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3-4 osteoarthritis (or avascular necrosis or RA-related joint-space narrowing), AND a documented 12-week (or 24-week if BMI>40 or age<50) trial of conservative therapy including anti-inflammatories, exercise, activity modification, and in-person supervised physical therapy. Unicompartmental knee arthroplasty has its own, more restrictive criteria requiring single-compartment disease and an intact ACL.
limitations: ing pain and disability from osteoarthritis, RA, avascular necrosis, or post-traumatic arthritis, plus limited ROM/crepitus/effusion on exam, plus radiographic Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3-4 osteoarthritis (or avascular necrosis or RA-related joint-space narrowing), AND a documented 12-week (or 24-week if BMI>40 or age<50) trial of conservative therapy including anti-inflammatories, exercise, activity modification, and in-person supervised physical therapy
